root_geometry.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
root_geometry.exact_pattern: Phi(root) == hub_residual_popcount(root) == ell + 1, for all five roots; direct arithmetic consequence of the root construction (extra w1 rotation steps visit extra hub-hexagon slots without changing P), not a new theorem
root_geometry.mergeability: the five roots are pairwise distinct at both raw and canonical-decorated-hash level (5 distinct values each); Round 38's decision NOT to merge them on shared resource signature is corroborated, not revisited

prune_histograms.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
prune_histograms.zero_count_reasons_note: H_positive, N_exceeded_monotone, and F1_fragment_normal_form_impossible never fire at any of the five roots; N_exceeded_monotone's zero count is a direct corollary of the r_count=0 finding below (Ndef cannot move without an R edge, and no R edge is ever enqueued), not independent information

recurring_dead_end_motif.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
recurring_dead_end_motif.statement: the only dead-end motif touching R-type edges in this data is R_event_not_eligible_r_count: every R-kind macro edge generated from an r_count=0 state is rejected by is_target_a_edge because r_count_before != 1 (Target A requires the SECOND R). No other geometry-specific dead-end pattern appears in the prune histogram.

ch1_ch2_distribution.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
ch1_ch2_distribution.statement: cannot be observed from this data: 0 of the 120103-134378 frontier states at any root have r_count > 0, so no state has taken an R event yet and the CH1/CH2 branch is undetermined at every single frontier state -- not because it is balanced, but because it is entirely unreached in this checkpoint data.

hub_completer_timing.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
hub_completer_timing.statement: the hub hexagon can reach full completion (popcount 6) purely through Z2/Z3 preserving/opening moves, with zero R events, in about 2.1% of the sampled depth-11/12 Q1 frontier; one example trajectory completes the hub by the walk's second macro edge (depth ~5 counting the abandonment root edge)
hub_completer_timing.caveat: this says nothing about which edge later serves as the CH1/CH2 completer -- only that hexagon-fill and R-event timing are not coupled the way the completer's eventual role might suggest

phi_and_m_trajectories.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
phi_and_m_trajectories.statement: M moves +1 on every Z2 edge and -4 on every Z3 edge, confirming (not re-proving) the Round 37 conservation law; Phi is flat across every rot^5 macro edge and drops by exactly (ell_run-5) on any shorter rotation run, matching (not re-deriving) the sawtooth already proven in research/SHORTFALL_BUDGET_THEOREM.md section 2

first_unavoidable_defect.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
first_unavoidable_defect.statement: 100% of frontier states at all five short roots have r_count=0. This is not a timeout artifact -- search_rr_target_a_unified.py lines 452-469 unconditionally `continue` past every R-kind macro edge regardless of r_count_before, so no R-transition child state is ever appended to the frontier. For the 28 long-excursion roots (root_r_count=1 already) this is correct: Target A needs exactly one more R event there, decided on the spot by is_target_a_edge. For the five short roots (root_r_count=0, k=2 R events needed), the FIRST R event must transition r_count 0->1 and continue, but the code discards it unconditionally -- so the r_count=1 subspace, the only place a Target A boundary can live for these roots, is provably unreachable by this traversal at any depth, for any time budget.
first_unavoidable_defect.code_citation: src/search_rr_target_a_unified.py lines 452-469 (the `if k == "R": ... continue` block) and line 337-345 (`is_target_a_edge`'s `if r_count_before != 1: return None`)
first_unavoidable_defect.empirical_confirmation: r_count distribution {0: n} at all five roots, n = queued_frontier_at_stop per root (see frontier_structure above)
first_unavoidable_defect.classification: completeness gap in the Round 36 traversal engine as applied to root_r_count=0 roots, not a soundness bug: every reported number (found_boundary_count=0, status=INCOMPLETE_TIMEOUT) remains literally true of what was explored; the gap is that the explored region provably excludes the only region a boundary could be in
first_unavoidable_defect.consequence_for_codex: stated as an observation about requirements only, not an instruction: a traversal that reuses this engine's R-edge handling verbatim will inherit the identical gap; a traversal that independently continues through the first R event for r_count=0 roots is unaffected by this finding. This document has no visibility into Codex's implementation.

proposal.label: CLAUDE_PROPOSAL
proposal.statement: treat an R-kind edge from an r_count_before==0 state as a normal continuable transition (append child with r_count=1 to the frontier, subject to the same q1_safe_prune_reason filter Z2/Z3 children already receive) instead of unconditionally discarding it; keep R-kind edges from r_count_before==1 states terminal exactly as today. This is a traversal-completeness change, not a new prune -- it restores reachability rather than shrinking the search space.

hand_proof.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
hand_proof.claim: the proposal (i) introduces no false positive and (ii) removes exactly the gap identified in first_unavoidable_defect, no more
argument: 1. No false positive: is_target_a_edge (the recognizer) is unchanged by the proposal; it still requires F_def==1, H==0, same-component, and r_count_before==1 exactly before reporting a hit, so the proposal (which only adds a traversal edge) cannot manufacture an accepted hit the existing recognizer would reject.

2. No unsound prune reuse: the four Q1-safe reasons (F_exceeded, H_positive, N_exceeded_monotone, F1_fragment_normal_form_impossible) are each proven monotone via dF/dH/dNdef case analysis that does not depend on which macro-edge kind produced the child, so applying them to the one newly continuable R-child is licensed by the existing proofs already in PRUNE_CLASSIFICATION.

3. No infinite regress: r_count_exceeded(nr)=nr>2 already fires identically regardless of edge kind, so a third R event remains excluded exactly as today; the proposal adds only the single missing r_count 0->1 transition.

4. Removes exactly the gap: since an RR word has at most two R events (Round 33/35, restated in r_count_exceeded's own docstring), a short-root Target A boundary, if one exists, is necessarily preceded by exactly one prior R event; (1)-(3) show the added transition is sound and the only change, so the r_count=1 subspace becomes reachable and only that subspace.
hand_proof.does_not_establish: that a Target A boundary exists at any short root -- only that a traversal built this way would be capable of finding one if it does
